# 0113 — ISF record interface ports reuse packed type and writer contracts

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Type: ISF language, lowering and public report contract
- Status: bounded input/output authoring admitted; complete output/consumer qualification remain open
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.2`

## Context

The preserved SPECFORGE request is `docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/packet.json`.
Its required R1–R3 ask for declared packed record inputs/outputs, scalar field access, whole
same-type port/storage copies, and visible type/layout metadata. R4 list-root ports and R5 variant
records are optional. The intake's current refusals are historical evidence, not a new regression
oracle after delivery.

At selection, the parser admitted aggregate aliases only on storage variables. Lowering already
preserves interface type references in `+size`; core `.fsm` type/path machinery owns packed
representation. Generated internal storage handoffs do not establish authored aggregate-port
support. Decisions `0107` and `0109` retain state ownership, physical writer admission and execution
qualification. R13/R14 require stable public reports and ordered IAL1 → IAL0 lowering; this feature
must not add a second type system or bypass IAL0.

## Decision

### Source and value contract

Select `(input NAME (type T))` and `(output NAME (type T))` for an existing actor-local or imported
package-qualified alias resolving to a packed record. Reuse the existing recursive record/list
member type system, including nested members. Root list ports remain R4. Unknown types, malformed
declarations, unresolved/nonpacked types and unsupported carriers fail before successful lowering,
with the port/type/context identified. Width/type exclusivity, closed options, declaration presence
and existing domain ownership remain. Typed output reset/default options remain outside this request
and retain their current explicit refusal.

Input fields are live scalar reads in each already-supported scalar expression context: transaction
conditions, set/update RHS, rules and named drives. Existing explicit sampling remains the way to
request a snapshot. Resolve paths against the declared root type; unknown members, non-scalar leaves
and out-of-range nested items fail contextually. Do not infer fields by punctuation or admit
whole-record truthiness, arithmetic or subaggregate writes.

Whole copies involving a record port require the same resolved record type: compare recursive kind,
member names/order and scalar width/signed/state-model properties under the existing type resolver;
equal packed width alone is insufficient. Alias spelling may differ when it resolves to that same
type. Support input-to-storage and storage-to-output, then other port/storage directions whose
declared input/output roles permit the read/write. Inputs cannot become assignment targets. Preserve
existing storage-only packed transfers and scalar-port behavior; the new check applies to
record-port copies, not retroactively to all aggregate storage assignments.

Reuse typed `+size` and explicit `+interface` carrier entries. Record member order is authored
order, first member most significant, as already implemented by
`AggregatePathSupport::record_member_low_offset`. Scalar paths retain their leaf widths and exact
packed ranges. No scalarized public field pins, payload register copies, implicit reset, added
pipeline edge or silent arbitration.

### Detached public metadata

Select optional `source.interface_ports` on successful directly parsed ISF check/semantic reports,
and `interface_ports` in schedule JSON. One producer must project fresh JSON-safe values from parsed
declared ports through native, API and actual newline MCP; it must not export parser/private IR
objects. Unrelated source formats and failure reports gain no invented ISF declarations. Unknown
declaration metadata in caller-created actors remains null, rather than reconstructed from inferred
hardware signals.

The snapshot orders inputs in their authored order followed by outputs in their authored order,
matching the existing parser handoff. Entries contain `name`, `direction`, `width`, and optional
authored `type` and resolved `type_kind`; named-domain entries also contain `domain`. A record adds
`fields`, an ordered array of scalar leaves with port-relative `path`, `width`, `lsb`, `msb`,
`signed`, and optional `state_model`. Nested paths follow the existing aggregate path syntax. The
normalized semantic type catalog remains the authority for recursive type declarations. Schedule
domain details carry the same snapshot for their declared ports. Generated private handoffs do not
appear as authored top ports. Advertise every added field family in the public capability contracts
and qualify detached values and complete report parity.

### Delivery and qualification order

1. Implement the detached metadata producer on the currently admitted scalar
   interface, with record-layout producer controls. Prove unchanged scheduled
   FSM and HDL; this preparatory slice does not admit record source ports.
2. Admit and qualify packed record inputs, scalar reads and input-to-storage
   whole copies. Cover local/imported/nested types, invalid paths/types, unused
   declarations, domains and generated children under their existing bounds.
3. Admit output records and whole copies only with sound physical writer
   ownership/admission, preserving unrelated scalar and storage controls.
4. Add scalar output-field writes after qualifying physical packed-range
   overlap. Whole-root/member overlap and generated competing writers must
   refuse unless a demonstrated compatibility/exclusion contract admits them.
5. Qualify affected backend profiles and the complete supplied consumer
   outcome. Direct SystemVerilog/Verilog and supported VHDL subsets have
   separate obligations; an unsupported profile must refuse precisely.

Input delivery does not depend on general independent-controller repairs. Output writes consume
those prerequisites only where their actual behavior needs them. Native HDL observations require
existing HIAL admission and failure-only observation; never replay a spent capture to seek
recurrence. Each implementation leaf may split further before source changes.

## Consequences at selection

R1–R3 remain unshipped until their owned slices and consumer qualification pass. R4/R5 stay
separately owned optional follow-ups after required duration/timer work; transaction-local aggregate
ports, banks and variant syntax are not implicitly admitted. The book keeps present support
boundaries and labels this selection as future work. No external corpus counts, timing guarantees,
runtime signoff or downstream integration completion follow from this decision.

Permanent qualification must include independently authored packed values, member-order/type
mismatch and input-write negatives, unchanged baseline controls, complete native/API/newline
products, supported corpus cases, capability/spec/book alignment and recoverable downstream response
evidence.

## Producer implementation evidence — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.1` qualifies the detached producer independently of source admission and report
wiring. T1983 retains independently expected nested/imported ranges, signed/state-model leaves,
mutation isolation and invalid metadata. The draft's hostile controls found an argument-context
defect: a failed regex returns an empty list in list context, while an array returns its members.
Either can change the predicate/message argument slots of a validation helper. Predicates now return
explicit booleans or scalar counts; the helper also requires exact argument arity. This is a
producer repair, not a claim about uninspected validators or a public record-port implementation.

Reproduce the failed-regex mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -e 'sub predicate { $_[0] =~ /\A[01]\z/ } sub guard { print "arguments=",scalar(@_)," first=",($_[0] // "undef"),"\n" } guard(predicate(2), "error message"); guard(scalar(predicate(2)), "error message");'
```

The first call places the message in the predicate slot; the scalar call keeps both slots. The
permanent hostile controls verify refusal rather than accepting report parity as proof of valid
metadata. No native HDL runtime is established.

and failed source reports omit the ISF source field.

The shipped preparatory surfaces are success `source.interface_ports`, schedule `interface_ports`
and owned `clock_domains[].interface_ports`, with one complete shared discovery descriptor at
`source_optional_fields.interface_ports` and `schedule_report_interface_ports`. T1984 independently
expects local/imported scalar declarations, unused/undriven entries, source order and domain
ownership; actual event crossings and generated children demonstrate private-port exclusion. This
report delivery does not admit authored records. Complete transport and supported-corpus
qualification remains explicitly owned by `.60.4.3.1.3` before record input implementation. No
native HDL runtime is claimed.

## Record-input ingress selection — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.1` traces the refused input boundary before widening it. Parser
`_finalize_actor_type_references` admits aggregate aliases only on storage;
`_validate_actor_aggregate_storage_paths`, rule operand maps and enum disambiguation currently
select storage roots. Adding inputs to one map is insufficient. Use a shared declaration-root
description, with transaction locals/formals and drive parameters masking outer names in their
actual scope. An input shadowed by a writable formal must not become that formal's role; an
unresolved local must not borrow its outer type or placeholder width. The existing formal resolver
and domain ownership remain authoritative.

Prepare a strict resolved-record identity gate separately from
`PayloadTypeSupport::payload_compatible_with_type_spec`. That public helper intentionally checks
payload shape and scalar width, allowing different signed and state-model facts. Preserve it for its
existing callers. Port copies compare recursive kinds, ordered record members, ordered list
children, widths, signed values and optional resolved state-model presence/value. Unspecified stays
unspecified; do not substitute a backend rendering default. Alias names are not part of resolved
identity. Malformed/unresolved roots fail contextually.

Transaction conditions, switch values, set/update RHS, rule guards/assignments, named-drive
bodies/actuals and inline drives need explicit scalar-versus-copy checks from the first admission.
Whole-record values are permitted only in qualified same-type assignments with allowed declaration
roles; expression operators, truthiness and subaggregate writes refuse. Existing storage-only packed
transfers retain their separate contract. Domain lookup resolves a path to its declared root,
honoring lexical masking and preserving the authored path in diagnostics; it must not invent a
crossing from a same-named formal.

The current aggregate validator handles `set`, but not `update` or `sample` leaf paths. Sampling
width collection copies exact root widths, not resolved leaf facts. Input delivery therefore owns
explicit scalar-leaf sampling in entry/body contexts, with resolved width/type and existing capture
timing. Whole-record sampling into an inferred alias remains outside this bounded delivery. No
hidden sample, delayed edge or new aggregate local is introduced. Typed `+size` and explicit
`+interface` already preserve unused declarations; generated/domain routes must retain those
identities before behavior signoff.

my $a = $p->parse_source(q{(actor controls
  (types (type plain (record (payload (bits 8)))) (type alias plain)
    (type signed_frame (record (payload (signed (bits 8)))))

The input lane now separately owns closed gates, source admission, generated/ domain carriers and
independent HDL/public completion. This planning receipt does not establish new input acceptance,
sampling support or native behavior.

## Unwired value-gate qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.2` prepares `ISFRecordPortValues` without parser or scheduler wiring.
`record_value_scope` takes closed resolved outer/local declarations; the nearest binding masks its
outer type and role even when unresolved. `record_value_reference` retains scalar path
type/width/range through `AggregatePathSupport`, refuses input writes and whole/subaggregate scalar
values, and returns unknown tokens to their existing validator. The caller must still validate those
tokens and supply actual lexical bindings; a prepared map does not establish parser, domain or
generated-child integration.

`validate_record_port_copy` uses the existing composition declared-type comparison after closed
resolved-shape validation by the qualified declaration producer. Root aliases are absent from that
identity. Equal packed widths, renamed/reordered members, bit/bits kinds, nested shape/list order,
signed and optional state-model differences are independently distinguished. Transfers with no whole
record port keep their existing scalar/storage assignment owner. Scalar formal/local slices use a
one-member wrapper for existing core traversal; the wrapper preserves offsets and adds no source
carrier or type declaration.

T1986's draft negative helper matched an expected regex passed as a caller argument inside

the resolver's `code`), yielding `unresolved` for otherwise specific invalid paths. Restricting the

producer now retains the core code. A permanent independently wrong message with the expected
pattern only in its stack demonstrates the original false match and the corrected oracle's
rejection. This is a repaired unshipped draft and test-helper defect, not a finding about
uninspected diagnostic oracles.

T1986 retains resolved alias/imported positives, independently authored ranges, same-width
counterexamples, lexical unresolved/scalar/formal shadows, input-role negatives, malformed/cyclic
facts, storage-only bypass and unchanged aggregate source refusal. T1983/T1259 and core path,

carriers, complete public products and HDL behavior remain owned by later leaves.

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.1` splits actual lexical/contextual gate preparation, explicit leaf sampling
carriers, declared-domain protection, first input admission and frontend/public replay before
implementation. Parser type finalization precedes aggregate/enum checks, but their current maps
select storage roots. Locals, formals, drive parameters and explicit samples require their actual
binding facts; inferred writes must not redefine an actor input. Sampling preparation must retain

or whole-record inferred local.

At pre-repair revision `02827d840254d6cdbfa4020be7910bb7ae9ac4cb`, public parse/lower probes reject
